transcript: A marriage without intimacy isn't just frustrating, it's dangerous. When intimacy disappears, the connection goes with it. There are no caresses, no closeness, no emotional security. Intimacy isn't just something physical. It's peace of mind, it's bonding, it's the way two people keep choosing each other. When affection dies out, the marriage slowly becomes two roommates paying bills. They stop building together. They stop hugging when leaving. They stop seeking each other out. Silence replaces affection. The more the relationship cools down, the weaker communication becomes. Trust disappears and desire fades away. It's not a small problem. The lack of intimacy becomes resentment, insecurities, emotional disconnection. And this is the truth no one wants to accept. A man who doesn't feel desired stops trying. A woman who doesn't feel valued starts pulling away. Little by little love becomes habit and not connection. Marriages almost never end because of big fights. They end by growing distant in silence. Write truth in the comments if this touched you. But I want you to understand something. Most people don't lose intimacy because they stopped loving. They lose it because they're exhausted. Daily stress kills desire. When you come home destroyed after working, worrying, enduring, you have nothing left to give. The body is tense. The mind is racing. The energy is gone. And the first thing that disappears when you're at your limit is the ability to connect. It's not that you don't love your partner. It's that your body has nothing left to give. Anxiety closes the body. Stress kills libido. Accumulated emotions create an invisible wall between the two. That's why there are couples who love each other and no longer touch. Because love remains but the body and mind can no longer. And if you want to recover the calm, you need to connect again. To feel desire once more. And for your relationship to stop growing cold. I've been learning in silence for over 20 years how to do it. And everything I know is inside the path back to calm. The link is in my profile.
